pullQuote.title: As good as gold
pullQuote.quote: The new Lucky wedges look and feel great and strike pure! I always play better when I feel Lucky!

buyBody: Forged 1020, a face that spins it out of anything, and gold you'll get asked about on the first tee. Six lofts, two grinds, right or left hand.

four.v: Send it back if it isn't the one

whatYouGet: One Carver 01 Gold wedge in the loft and hand you picked
Lucky Golf stock steel shaft (KBS becomes an option soon)
No headcover (none of our clubs ship with one)
carePara: The gold finish is a finish, not a coating you have to baby, but grooves full of sand don't spin anything. Brush the face after a round and dry the head before it goes back in the bag.
A headcover is worth it if your clubs rattle around in the cart. Several reviewers mention picking up cart rash without one.
marquee: Six lofts, right and left hand
_club: Fourth pass, 2026-08-19. Cole: 'I feel like you're using the same structure over and over again.' He was right: every intro opened material -> 'so it feels' -> feature -> 'so it' -> spec line. Takomo's intros each open through a different door (a situation, a joke, a problem, a brag, a sibling). THIS ONE OPENS WITH: the shot.
clubHeadline: Forged feel meets filthy spin. Rip it back and go tap it in.
clubParas: Hit one a little thin out of wet rough and watch it still check up. That's the dual-texture face: it grips the ball everywhere, not just in the grooves, so the spin shows up on the shots you didn't catch pure. The head is forged from 1020 carbon steel, which is why it feels buttery when you do catch one and tells you the truth when you don't. Six lofts, two grinds, and you can build the exact short game your bag is missing.

clubGrinds.v: A wider, flatter sole with a standard leading edge. Set up square, take your divot, get the same result every time. Built for standard lies: fairway, rough, fringe. All six lofts.
A narrower, relieved sole with a reshaped leading edge, so the face opens without the bounce fighting you. Built for tight lies, bunker shots and open-face lobs. 52, 56 and 60.

clubSpecs.v: High spin in any conditions, soft feel, honest feedback on every strike.
Forged 1020 head with a dual-texture face: CNC-milled grooves, micro-milled between, sandblasted across.
Any golfer. If your chips don't stop, start here.

_signoff:
GRIND COPY — sourced, no longer a draft.
1. SOURCE IS THE SPEC-TO-BENEFIT TRANSLATION GUIDE v1.0 (Cole supplied it 2026-08-01, references-spec-to-benefit-v1.0.md). It defines both grinds directly: K is "a wider, flatter sole profile with a standard leading edge... the no-surprises wedge... built for the golfer who strikes cleanly and plays primarily from standard lies"; S is "a narrower, more relieved sole with a reshaped leading edge... the versatility wedge... tight lies, awkward angles, open-face lobs".
2. THIS REVERSES AN EARLIER CORRECTION. HANDOFF §24d recorded that the S is NOT the open-face versatility grind, on the basis that our letters are Vokey's and that is Vokey's M. Lucky's own written guide says otherwise, and a company document about what Lucky's specs mean outranks an inference from another maker's nomenclature. The site now follows the guide. If Cole wants the Vokey reading back, this is the block to change.
3. IT ALSO CLOSES §24a's open question. "Is our S actually narrower, does it have a tapered rear sole" is answered in writing: narrower, more relieved, reshaped leading edge. This block is no longer the unverified one.
4. Every number in `facts` is still the manufacturer sheet, and the measured-vs-effective bounce note still stands — a narrow relieved sole carrying more measured bounce than a wide flat one is exactly what the geometry predicts.
_specTabs: Takomo-shaped 2026-08-18 at Cole's instruction: three tabs (Clubs / Shafts / Grips), each ONE card = caption, short key/value head, black-header matrix. Better than theirs in one way: K and S get their own rows instead of '10F / 12V' crammed in a cell. Every number is the Product Reference Guide's. NO swing weight, tip diameter, grip length/core: the guide does not publish them and they are not invented. GRIP: one row, Regular, 55 g (Cole 2026-08-18; the 2 g K/S difference is not worth a second row). FINISH: plain 'Gold', no link (Cole 2026-08-18: the finish swatches are one scroll up in the buy box). BOUNCE/GRIND: exactly Takomo's shape, ONE row, 'K / S' in a cell where both exist. Lie the same way, in the matrix not the head. Head block is Head material / Face / Finish only, stacked vertically. BOUNCE: Takomo's suffix notation (8F) adopted with OUR letters (8K, 10S) so the matrix matches the picker's 52K / 52S.
_rest: Rest-of-page pass 2026-08-19 (HANDOFF 37g): buy body, sub-blocks, bullets, spec head, look, helper, close, each written as the person and each opening through a different door from the other four clubs. The buy bodies no longer end 'sixty days to decide' (the trust row under the button says it). The closes no longer all end 'Sixty days to decide' (the close trust row says it).
_weight: Cole 2026-08-19: do not write that the wedge weighs the same at every loft. The 300 g row stays in the spec matrix (it is the manufacturer's sheet, and the table is data) but no copy is built on it, and no 'they all feel like the same club' line derives from it. The Design bullet's 'Weighting shifts by loft' also came off: unsourced, and it contradicted the sheet it sits above.
_photo: Real photography from the 2026 course shoot, chosen from Cole's archive 2026-08-23, resized to 2048px and uploaded to Shopify Files. The `photo` brief stays in the file: it is the record of what the slot asked for, and it renders again if photoSrc is ever removed.
_video: Video REMOVED 2026-08-23 at Cole's instruction: he will hand-pick the clips himself later. The template and JS keep the conditional (videoSrc / reel[].src), so dropping the keys back in is all it takes. The files are still in Shopify Files if he wants those exact ones.
